summary: All tests pass. The needle was in `app/auth.py:150-152` — `check_admin_access` compared a BIDI-*rendered* display name (which reverses text after `U+202E`) against the admin allowlist instead of the actual stored username. This let an attacker register as `\u202enimda` — stored as-is, but visually rendered "admin" — and get granted admin access. Fixed by checking the raw stored `username` directly against `ADMIN_USERS`. `./test.sh` now reports `PASS` for all cases.
